messages:
akira: CI microbench on PR #15234 failed on merge build — observed +7.4% 99th tail latency vs main. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.internal/15234/artifacts (perf diff, flamegraphs, raw traces). Failing test: perf/microbench/kv_warmup_hitrate.test.

ci-bot: perf/microbench/kv_warmup_hitrate.test exceeded threshold. baseline=12.3ms new=13.25ms delta=+7.4% (threshold 3%). Build: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/7721.

liam: :eyes: which commit landed in that build? any other recent runtime changes?

akira: The big one is the kernel-autoselect refactor merged yesterday (commit 9c1d3a7). It also touched batch sampler entropy and kv warmup weighting.

priya: I fetched the artifact and ran a quick perf sample. Coldpath shows a concentrated hotspot in kernel_selector::getKernelScore() after the refactor. Stack sample and top symbols:
```
# Samples: 1K of event 'cpu-clock'
- kernel_selector::getKernelScore (45%)
- runtime::dispatch (12%)
- kv_cache::lookup (8%)
```
Haven't dug into why the score change increases tail latency but it's the suspicious place.

tom: Can you repro locally on staging? Try forcing the previous heuristic with `RW_KERNEL_AUTOPICK=0` to see if it regresses back.

akira: Repro'd on staging with the same microbench seed. With autopick enabled: 99p=13.2ms. With `RW_KERNEL_AUTOPICK=0`: 99p=12.2ms (within baseline). Repro commands I used: 
```
# staging repro
./tools/run_microbench --test kv_warmup_hitrate --seed 42 --concurrency 8
# disable new kernel autopick
RW_KERNEL_AUTOPICK=0 ./tools/run_microbench ...
```
So disabling new heuristic restores perf.

maya: :warning: this looks like a rollout blocker. We should hold the rollout / pause canaries until we either fix or revert.

rachel: Can we add a unit/perf regression test that covers kernel selection + kv warmup pattern? I'll put a TODO on the perf harness: deterministic seed + synthetic warmup profile.

devx: Do we have a hotfix PR ready, or should we revert the refactor? Which is faster?

liam: I ran a git-bisect across the merge window, narrowed it down — culprit is indeed 9c1d3a7. Bisect snippet: 
```
$ git bisect log
9c1d3a7 is the first bad commit
commit 9c1d3a7
Author: Priya <priya@redwood>
Date:   Thu Mar 14
    runtime: refactor kernel autoselect and sampler weighting
```

akira: OK I'm opening a revert PR for 9c1d3a7 now (will target staging first). Kicking CI.

ci-bot: Revert PR #15299 created to revert commit 9c1d3a7. CI queued: https://ci.redwood.internal/15299.

maya: Thanks. I'm putting the release on hold and notifying PMs that canaries are paused.

liam: Post-merge action items: add a microbench test to detect kernel-score regressions, and add an opt-in flag for the new heuristic behind a feature flag.

akira: Agreed. After revert verifies green, we'll rework weighting and add the regression test before re-landing.

rachel: I'll own the perf test and add it to the CI perf-suite gating thresholds.

devx: Noted — will update the release notes and unblock when CI passes.

ci-bot: CI for revert PR #15299 started. Test perf/microbench/kv_warmup_hitrate.test running...
